'''David Bakradze''' ({{lang-ka|დავით ბაქრაძე}}; born 1 July 1972) is a [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] politician and diplomat who served as the Chairman of the [[Parliament of Georgia]] from 7 June 2008 to 21 October 2012.

Bakradze's previous assignments include a member of the Parliament from the [[United National Movement (Georgia)|United National Movement]] (April 2004-September 2007), Minister for the Conflict Issues (July 2007-January 2008), Minister of Foreign Affairs (January 2008-April 2008), and the President of Georgia's special envoy to [[NATO]] and the [[European Union]] (April 2008-June 2008). He is a [[First Class (European Union)|First Class]] [[Councillor|State Counselor]] and holds a [[diplomatic rank]] of [[Minister-counselor|Chief Minister Counselor]].

==Early life and education==
David Bakradze was born in [[Tbilisi]], [[Georgian SSR]]. He was educated at [[Georgian Technical University]] and the Georgian Institute for Public Affairs ([[Georgian Institute of Public Affairs|GIPA]]) as well as gaining a Doctor's degree in Physics and Mathematics from [[Tbilisi State University]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2009}} Apart from numerous high-profile government positions Bakradze has been actively involved in various educational programmes attending the Swiss International Relations Institute in [[Geneva]], in 1997, and studying at George Marshall European Centre for Security Studies in [[Germany]] in 1998. In 2001 Bakradze graduated from [[NATO Defence College]], [[Rome]], [[Italy]]. He has served in the [[National Guard of Georgia]] Reserve and is a [[lieutenant commander]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2009}}

== Political career ==
Bakradze has been actively involved in Georgian politics since 1997. He worked for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia from 1997 to 2002, and for the [[National Security Council of Georgia]] from 2002 to 2004. In April 2004, he was elected to the [[Parliament of Georgia]] from the [[United National Movement (Georgia)|United National Movement]] (UNM) led by the [[President of Georgia]] [[Mikheil Saakashvili]]. He chaired the Parliamentary Committee for the [[European Union|Euro]]-[[NATO|Atlantic]] Integration until 19 July 2007, when he was appointed as a Minister for the Conflict Issues, and hence, a chief negotiator in the [[Abkhazia]]n and [[South Ossetia]]n affairs. In January 2008, he became the Foreign Minister of Georgia in the cabinet of the [[Prime Minister of Georgia|Prime Minister]] [[Lado Gurgenidze]].

On 21 April 2008 Bakradze was named to lead the UNM [[party list]] in the [[2008 Georgian legislative election|parliamentary election]] scheduled on 21 May 2008. This decision came after the chairperson of the outgoing parliament, [[Nino Burjanadze]], refused, in a surprise move, to lead the party list due to her disagreement with the UNM leadership.<ref>[https://www.rferl.org/a/1109610.html Georgia: In Surprise Move, Burjanadze Says She Won't Seek Reelection]. [[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty]]. April 22, 2008.</ref>

On 7 June 2008 Bakradze was unanimously elected a chairperson of the Parliament of Georgia at that legislature's inaugural session.<ref>[http://civil.ge/eng/article.php?id=18498 Bakradze Elected as New Parliamentary Chairman] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110521095043/http://civil.ge/eng/article.php?id=18498 |date=2011-05-21 }}. Civil Georgia. 2008-06-07.</ref> In 2012 he was again selected again selected to lead the UNM list for the 1 October [[2012 Georgian parliamentary election|parliamentary election]], which was won by the [[Bidzina Ivanishvili]]-[[Georgian Dream]] opposition coalition. Consequently, Bakradze became the leader of the parliamentary minority, being succeeded by [[David Usupashvili]], a Georgian Dream member, as the chairman of the parliament.<ref>[https://civil.ge/eng/article.php?id=25376 New Parliament Speaker Elected]. Civil Georgia. October 21, 2012.</ref>

In 2013, Bakradze was selected to be the UNM's candidate through internal party election, primaries for the 27 October [[2013 Georgian presidential election|presidential election]]. He ended up second in the race and, shortly after the exit poll results were announced, congratulated Georgian Dream's candidate [[Giorgi Margvelashvili]] on victory.<ref>[https://www.civil.ge/eng/article.php?id=26621 UNM's Bakradze Congratulates GD's Margvelashvili]. Civil Georgia. October 27, 2013.</ref> In the [[2018 Georgian presidential election|2018 election]], he came in third and received nearly 11 percent of the vote; for the [[Two-round system|run-off]], he announced he would support [[Grigol Vashadze]] in the second round.<ref>Margarita Antidze (October 29, 2018), [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-georgia-election/georgia-presidential-vote-heads-for-runoff-in-setback-for-ruling-party-idUSKCN1N30PB Georgia presidential vote heads for runoff in setback for ruling party] ''[[Reuters]]''.</ref>

==Recognition==
Bakradze was awarded the Commander's Cross Order of Merit of the Republic of Poland by the President of Poland (2010).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.prezydent.pl/aktualnosci/ordery-i-odznaczenia/art,809,order-dla-przewodniczacego-parlamentu-gruzji.html |title=Order dla Przewodniczącego Parlamentu Gruzji / Ordery i odznaczenia / Aktualności / Oficjalna strona Prezydenta Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej |access-date=2011-03-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928123537/http://www.prezydent.pl/aktualnosci/ordery-i-odznaczenia/art,809,order-dla-przewodniczacego-parlamentu-gruzji.html |archive-date=2011-09-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
